what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Bit Cloud's records ran out where sgit fits
sections.para: On 11 October The New Stack published Ignacio Aldama's demo: a fresh Claude Code session found a shared ticket contract in two MCP calls and left it alone. He named where the records ran out: structure not behaviour, skipped tests, demo shortcuts, unversioned memory. Those edges are where sgit and RiskMandate sit.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Each gap the demo named has a fix here
sections.para: A fresh session called read_scope and read_components, found a shared ticket entity, changed only the app, and 41 tests passed. The named gaps map to RiskMandate labels: documented claims, expectations reported as boundaries, grants wider than the mandate. sgit keeps memory and records in one encrypted history and crosses company boundaries.

sections.label: What the article reports
sections.line: Two MCP calls found the contract, then records stopped
sections.para: Aldama, a Bit Cloud engineer, asked a fresh session to add ticket filtering to a four-component console. It found the app and service shared a ticket entity and implemented the filter in the app only. He then listed the gaps: an unchecked route list, skipped MongoDB tests, a public signing secret, and memory not tied to versions.

sections.label: Structure, not behaviour: label every fact with how it is known
sections.line: Label every fact by how it is known
sections.para: The route list was a documented claim that read like a fact. The abp.sgit.ai policy packs label rows as derived, inferred, self-reported, documented, measured or observed. Aldama's manual persistence check was observed. In an sgit vault the observation sits in the same history, and sgit check verify classifies each commit's signature.

sections.label: A green build is an expectation until the tests ran
sections.line: A skipped test is a control that never ran
sections.para: Only a boundary is a control, so a green build over a skipped required test reports an expectation as a control. The fix is to count the run from what happened, not the exit code, writing required, run, skipped and why into a vault. This is proposed, not built.

sections.label: Demo shortcuts: name the gap and accept it for an interval
sections.line: Accept demo shortcuts by name and interval, or stop
sections.para: A public signing secret and demo account are a grant wider than the mandate, which drifts into production. RiskMandate says the risk must be accepted by a named owner for an interval, or the activity stops. Unfinished items become licence-to-operate conditions. sgit pki keygen keeps keys local, and a leak scan runs before every commit.

sections.label: Memory and records in one versioned history
sections.line: One encrypted history ties intent to each version
sections.para: Memory holds intent but is not tied to versions; build records are versioned but hold no intent. sgit lets both sit in the same commit, so the intent of version 1.4 is recorded at 1.4. Because the host never sees names, contents or messages, sensitive intent can be written down at all.

sections.label: The other side of the dependency
sections.line: sgit publish, mirror and lanes cross company boundaries
sections.para: Aldama wants records that hold beyond the agent's index, which Nx and Sourcegraph do not offer across companies. sgit 0.21.0 documents publish, readable by clone over plain GETs, keyless verifiable mirrors, and append lanes for outside writers. Publish and mirror were not tested for this article.

sections.label: What the article does not say
sections.line: The agent's restraint was judgement, not an enforced boundary
sections.para: Nothing stopped the demo agent changing a contract two components depend on; leaving it alone was its own good sense. In policy terms that is a write row with a blast radius of two, held by an expectation. A platform holding the records could require approval to version a shared entity, making it a guarantee.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: One disclosed demo; some fixes are proposed or untested
sections.para: It is one demo by the platform's own engineer, who discloses it. The four edges are his findings, the labels are RiskMandate's. The green-build record is only proposed, and publish and mirror are documented but untested here. Records, memory, evidence and acceptance are four things that belong in one history.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Sources: Aldama's New Stack piece and sgit docs
sections.para: The answered article is Ignacio Aldama's piece in The New Stack, 11 October 2026, read in full. The piece began as a RiskMandate research note that day. sgit features come from the sgit-ai 0.21.0 README and changelog, alongside RiskMandate's acceptance, licence to operate and Agent Behaviour Policy pages and abp.sgit.ai.
